why.title: Why a family office should be led by an advocate
why.lead: A banker, an asset manager or an accountant can be compelled to disclose your correspondence to a court or regulator. An advocate cannot. It is the only profession for which client secrecy is not a privacy policy but a rule of law.

it.title: In-house IT development — inside advocate secrecy
it.lead: The family office platform is built and operated by the firm itself. Data, documents and the activity ledger are part of the advocate's case file, not a third-party contractor's service: they are protected by the same regime as a conversation with your advocate.

items.d: Every step — signing in, uploading a document, sending and opening a message — gets its own ID, time and device fingerprint and is added to a hash chain. No record can be altered unnoticed.
Two perimeters — privileged and operational. Role-based access with hardware keys, encryption of every document, download links that live five minutes, watermarks with name and time.
Privileged documents cannot be forwarded to third parties. NDAs with staff and contractors, information security audits, monitoring of personal data leaks.

Information covered by advocate secrecy cannot be demanded from the advocate, and the advocate cannot be questioned about it as a witness. Searches, inspections and seizures concerning an advocate require a court order and the presence of a bar chamber representative (Art. 8, Law 63-FZ; Art. 450.1, Russian Code of Criminal Procedure).

privilege.title: Two ambassadors — two letters
privilege.lead: The main weakness of any family office is mixed correspondence. When legal advice sits next to investment advice in one email, a court may strip protection from the whole document. The platform separates these flows by design.

rules.d: The privileged legal perimeter and the operational one for bankers, managers and staff are physically separated.
Before sending, the platform flags a commercial question inside a legal message and offers to split it in two.
The privilege legend goes on legal documents only — indiscriminate marking devalues protection.
Privileged documents cannot be forwarded to an outside manager — the most common way privilege is waived by accident.

canon.title: Design canon
canon.lead: The rules the platform is built on. Aristocracy lies in restraint: a museum engraving, a hairline rule, plenty of air and no gold for the sake of gold.
canon.pigmentsNote: Colours are named after Renaissance workshop pigments. There are no green pigments — statuses are coded with ultramarine, ochre and madder.
canon.typeNote: Cormorant Garamond for headings and quotations. Manrope for interface and figures. IBM Plex Mono for article numbers, hashes and references. All three support Cyrillic and Hungarian ő, ű.
artRules: Only authentic works from open collections — no generation
Engraving treatment: warm monochrome, no gilding
The detail beats the whole: hands, instruments, architecture
Every image carries a museum label
canon.dashNote: From banking apps we take the ergonomics: large figures, soft 24px cards, stories on top, bottom navigation on the phone. The difference: paper background, serif headings and a pigment palette.

ledger.title: Activity ledger
ledger.lead: Every action in the cabinets — signing in, uploading a document, sending and opening a message — gets its own ID, exact time, device and signature and is added to a hash chain. No record can be altered or deleted unnoticed: verification shows exactly where the chain breaks.
ledger.tampered: Record #{n} was altered outside the system (time shifted by one hour). The check below shows the break.
ledger.graphNote: Columns are participants, rows are events in order. The thin line is the hash chain, coloured arcs are causal links.
ledger.select: Select an event in the graph

how.title: How it works
items: UUIDv7 IDs are unique and time-ordered and are assigned to every step automatically.
Each record contains the SHA-256 of the previous one: changing one record breaks the whole chain after it — like a blockchain, but without a public network.
Causal links form a graph: “message opened” points to “message sent”, every action points to the sign-in and its device.
Sign-in is signed with a session key — in production, the user's hardware key (WebAuthn). Documents and texts never enter the ledger, only their hashes.

legal.title: Legal precision
legal.text: The Merkle root fixes the whole ledger in one hash. In production it is signed by the firm's server every hour, sealed with a qualified time stamp (eIDAS for Hungary and the EU, an accredited provider under Law 63-FZ for Russia) and stored in write-once storage. A statement on any event can be produced in court with an inclusion proof, without disclosing the rest of the ledger.
